name: Cenegermin
lead: Cenegermin (brand name Oxervate) is a recombinant human nerve growth factor (rhNGF) given as an eye drop, produced in E. coli. It acts on the TrkA and p75NTR receptors and was the first drug approved for neurotrophic keratitis, a rare condition in which damaged corneal nerves lead to persistent epithelial defects [4][8]. The European Union approved it in 2017 and the United States in 2018 [7].

In the registration trials, most adults with moderate or severe neurotrophic keratitis reached complete corneal healing within eight weeks, with healing rates generally higher than with vehicle [4]. The most common adverse effects are eye pain, inflammation, increased tearing, eyelid pain and a foreign-body sensation [7].

Cenegermin is a medical eye treatment and is not described in the sources as an appearance product. It is included in this wiki because it is a recovery-category biologic; the sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing community discussion.

paras: The approved indication is neurotrophic keratitis (also called neurotrophic keratopathy), in which reduced or absent corneal sensation impairs the trophic function of sensory nerves and leaves the epithelium prone to breakdown and the stroma to melting [1]. Existing treatments have mainly been supportive, and cenegermin was introduced to address the underlying nerve-related problem [3].

A multicenter, randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled trial (NGF0214) in 11 US sites randomized 48 patients with a neurotrophic persistent epithelial defect to cenegermin 20 micrograms per millilitre or vehicle, with six drops daily for eight weeks [2]. A Drugs review of the registration trials reported that most adults achieved complete healing after up to eight weeks, with higher rates than vehicle [4]. Follow-up reports have examined corneal nerves and sensitivity over eight months and longer-term clinical efficacy [9][10]. A NICE single technology appraisal evidence review assessed it from a cost-effectiveness perspective [11].
Common adverse effects reported are eye pain, ocular inflammation, increased tearing, eyelid pain and a feeling of a foreign body in the eye [7].

Beyond the pivotal randomized trial and its follow-ups above [2][9][10], ClinicalTrials.gov lists further registered studies: a recruiting phase 3 trial of intranasal cenegermin in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NCT07453888) [12], a phase 3 trial in persistent corneal epithelial defect (NCT07519902) [13], a completed phase 3 trial in severe Sjogren's dry eye disease (NCT05136170) [14], a completed phase 2 trial of rhNGF in moderate to severe dry eye (NCT03982368) [15], and a completed phase 4 study in stage 1 neurotrophic keratitis (NCT04485546) [16]. No studies of cenegermin for cosmetic or appearance purposes were found.
Cenegermin is prescription-only in the US, EU, Canada and Australia [7]. No looksmaxxing community use was documented in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: US FDA approval, described as first-in-class [7].
Pivotal NGF0214 trial published in Ophthalmology [2].

card.summary: A prescription nerve growth factor eye drop approved for a rare corneal disease, with no appearance use.
card.note: Approved only for neurotrophic keratitis; no cosmetic studies.

quick.overview:
Cenegermin (Oxervate) is a recombinant human nerve growth factor eye drop approved in the EU in 2017 and the US in 2018 for neurotrophic keratitis, a rare corneal nerve disease.

Trials in that condition showed most patients healing within about eight weeks. It is not an appearance product, and no cosmetic studies were found.
quick.mechanism: It acts on the TrkA and p75NTR receptors and was developed to address the nerve-related cause of corneal breakdown rather than only support the surface.
quick.risks: Reported adverse effects include eye pain, inflammation, tearing, eyelid pain and foreign-body sensation. It is prescription-only.
